parts.meaning: Before combat, the group declares whether its attacks are intended to kill or subdue. If no mode is announced, attacks take the killing form; after choosing a form, it cannot be changed for that dragon.

The source names dragon categories that cannot be subdued and says creatures with less than average intelligence cannot attack to subdue. Preserve this as source wording; do not reinterpret the category terms.

After subdual intent is declared, all hit-point damage from attacks on the dragon is nonfatal battering/bruising damage. This is a specific damage treatment, distinct from the current generic 75% temporary/25% real split.

At the end of each melee round, compare accumulated subdual damage with the dragon's total hit points and express the ratio as a percentage chance of subduing it; the worked example confirms damage is accumulated across rounds.
Roll percentile dice; a result equal to or below the percentage chance subdues the dragon. At a 1:1 ratio or higher (100% or more), subdual is automatic.
At most one human-sized attacker per three linear feet of exposed dragon body, excluding tail; a fully exposed 15-foot body gives 11 attackers (five along each flank plus one at the head).

The example carries damage forward against an 88-hit-point dragon: 44/88 gives 50%; then 67/88 about 76%; then 77/88 about 87.5% (the text says treat as 88%). A roll of 89 fails; after another 12 damage, 89/88 crosses 1:1 and subdues automatically. This confirms accumulated damage and the deterministic threshold.

The adjacent Length of Subdual paragraph says the subdued state can last indefinitely, but if the dragon is not strongly held, treated well, supplied with ample treasure and allowed freedom it seeks to kill/escape. Older, stronger dragons are less likely to remain subdued; intelligent spell-using dragons may try to take over. It also gives alignment-dependent behavior, including a 50% greater kill/escape likelihood for good dragons held by a neutral captor than by a same-alignment one, and says a dragon cannot be subdued again until it regains freedom.

findings.scopeAssessment: This is not only topical overlap: the exposed `rules/subdual` card expressly tells the reader to check eligibility and creature-specific rules. The MM p.30 procedure is a bounded rule that supplies exactly such a creature-specific resolution. The current rule has no MM p.30 control and does not reproduce these steps. README.md:85 does not expressly exclude a stand-alone procedure that supports an exposed rule, so do not close this as excluded merely because it appears in a monster article. Keep the full Dragon profile and breath-table work separate.
integrationCautions: Do not merge this with the DMG 75/25 generic damage split without preserving the MM statement that all damage during the declared dragon-subdual attempt is nonfatal battering/bruising.

The current generic card's sentence that the procedure does not apply to player characters is ambiguous as to whether PCs are targets or attackers; the MM worked example has player-character attackers. Any future wording should preserve that actor/target distinction. This review did not independently re-source-check DMG p.67 or propose changing that card.
The source's dragon category wording and percentage example are preserved as source-specific; no editorial normalization was made.
